page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a marginal note at the right beside the first paragraph. Below the text is a woodcut ornament (not text). Page number at the top centre. Stray marks at the left edge are not part of the page.

main_text.p: Illa[?] nubes est, ex qua siccus ille halitus elicitur: tonitrui non amplius ista, sed illa quæ icta est: quia sonitus ille quicquid Vulgus dicat, de sententia Philosophi, non elisio-ne fit, sed ictu, cum elisus ille halitus siue Spiritus in aliamLib.2.Me-teor.cap.6[?] nubem densam incidit: quo ictu tum sonus editur, tum Spiritus accenditur: quæ accensio tonitrui consectarium quoddam est.
Maris denique & salsæ illius aquæ subiectum concre-tum corpus est, quod è potiore parte elementi aquæ, & sicco illo, qui unà cum pluvia deorsum perpetuo fertur, halitu, constat.

Concludimus ergo, primum & adæquatum Meteorologicarum affectionum subiectum imperfectè mixtum corpus, quâ tale est, esse, idque ex uno è quatuor elementis & alterutro halitu concretum corpus esse: quod quatuor præcipuas sub se species comprehendit, concretionem è sicco illo halitu & elemento ignis, ex aere & alterutro halitu, è terra & alterutro halitu, ex aqua & halitu sicco[?],

page.notes: Woodcut ornament (a symmetrical floral/scroll fleuron) below the text; not transcribed. Long s was read as s throughout; the printed f in "elifus", "elifio-ne" and similar words is long s. "Illa" at the start is partly damaged and uncertain. The page number "9" is ornate and uncertain. The marginal reference's final digit is uncertain. The last word of the page is partly worn ("ficcq," read as sicco[?],). Stray marks at the left edge are the edge of the neighbouring page or show-through and were left out. The page ends mid-sentence, so there is no catchword.
